findings.F1: The test's slope is on the side the idea predicts but falls short of the bar (slope +0.00031, t 1.92, 5,683 grid cases). Half of those cases (2,873) have a forecast of 0 after a 24-hour rise. On the 2,810 cases with a positive forecast alone, the slope is +0.00069 with t 2.90.
findings.F2: The forecast scales the fall against the coin's last 60 hours, and that measures the idea poorly. Measured as the raw depth of the 24-hour fall, the same 72-hour excess return has a slope of 0.263 with t 6.04 over 2,720 falls. Scaled by the coin's 30-day hourly volatility, the slope is 0.0105 with t 4.32 over 2,516 falls.
findings.F3: The effect sits in the deepest falls only. Falls beyond -5 % in 24 hours (548 cases) are followed by a 72-hour excess return of +1.54 %, about 8 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. The four shallower fall quintiles are all negative (-0.16 % to -0.85 %). The deepest tenth of all cases earns +1.49 % (t 3.38, 556 cases).
findings.F4: The rebound is a 1-to-3-day effect that fades by a week. The deepest tenth earns +1.06 % over 24 hours (t 3.80) and +1.49 % over 72 hours (t 3.38). Over 168 hours it earns +1.19 % with t only 1.68. The test's own slope has t 3.93 at 24 hours and t 0.59 at 168 hours.
findings.F5: The effect is stronger when the coin's 30-day return is positive. There the raw-fall slope is 0.572 (t 5.84, 950 falls), and the deepest tenth earns +3.00 % over 72 hours (t 3.08, 163 cases). When the 30-day return is negative, the deepest tenth earns +0.98 % (t 1.80, 233 cases).

ideas.name: one-day fall, more coins
ideas.idea: The more a coin has fallen over its last 24 hours, the more it rises over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader buying after a deep one-day fall and holding for days captures a move several times a round trip, which the evening 2-hour trade cannot.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall over its last 24 hours, measured against its typical daily move over the last 30 days, the more it rises over the next 3 days, more so while its 30-day return is positive.
ideas.consequence: A trader buying a coin after an unusually deep one-day fall within a rising month and holding it for three days captures a rebound several times a round trip, while shallow dips give nothing to trade.
ideas.name: deep fall rebound in uptrend
